cases.prompt: Size the MuleSoft-to-Apigee migration for Lakeside Health. The assessor output says 118 interfaces: 60 simple, 40 medium, 18 complex. Our prior actuals (attached) give unit efforts per band. Rate card attached. Fixed price per wave. Give me P50/P80/P90, staffing, and price.
expected: WBS CSV built with parametric tasks (count x unit) citing the prior actuals as basis PAR, plus explicit PM, QA, environments, cutover, hypercare, KT packages
Runs scripts/estimate.py with the rate card; reports P50/P80/P90 and contingency as P80 - P50
Quotes P80 (fixed price, inventory known) and states why
Staffing table by role and phase with onshore/offshore split; allocations between 20% and 100%
Price computed only from the supplied rate card; margin at P50 and P80
Every count and unit effort is an assumption row with source
Memo follows assets/estimate-summary-template.md

cases.prompt: Here is the WBS. Give me the price.
expected: Asks once for the rate card (role, location, cost_rate, bill_rate, currency, valid_until)
Produces effort-only output (P50/P80/P90, staffing) in the meantime
Price shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]; no rates assumed or 'typical' rates used

cases.prompt: We have no actuals. Just use industry-standard effort per interface — I think it is about 3 days each — and give me a fixed price at P50 so we look competitive.
expected: Does not supply an 'industry-standard' unit effort; marks unit efforts as judgment with [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] for the anchor source, and uses the user's 3-day figure only if the user confirms it as their own assumption, labeled JUD
Flags basis mix JUD > 30% as low-confidence and recommends an assessment phase or per-unit pricing with a count band
Explains in one line why fixed price at P50 carries no contingency and recommends P80/P90 or T&M with NTE
Shows P50 and P80 side by side with contingency explicit
